clue.text: Cheats to hold on to bloodsuckers? Nonsense!

blocks.note: to fiddle is to cheat, as with accounts
ticks are parasites that feed on blood

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at the idea of swindlers clinging on to parasites.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old-fashioned exclamation dismissing something as rubbish, just like 'Nonsense!'

clue.text: Hand of airman moving round very quietly

indicators.note: something moving round another thing goes about it, so one piece encircles the other

blocks.note: a flier is a pilot or aviator
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A pilot's hand creeping silently around something.
explanation.walkthrough: pp, short for pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly; 'moving round' tells the airman to go around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipper is informal slang for a person's hand, from a seal's paddle-like limb.

clue.text: Forceful doctor, one no good after six

indicators.note: after puts the words just before it behind the word that follows, reversing their clue order

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
the Roman numeral for one
the Roman numeral for six
ng is the standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A pushy doctor, a single useless one, coming after six others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forceful doctor' looks like one unit, but the doctor is wordplay and only 'Forceful' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving as an adjective describes something with strong energy and force, such as driving rain or a driving ambition.

clue.text: Gruel, a lot, revived drunken hooligan

indicators.note: something revived is brought back in a new state, so these letters return reordered

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: Plenty of porridge brings a drunk back round.
explanation.walkthrough: A lager lout is British slang for a young man made rowdy and aggressive by beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lager lout is a youth who behaves aggressively after drinking too much beer, a drunken troublemaker.

clue.text: Sacks turned over in this armless chair

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to sack a town is to loot it; loots is the verb form

explanation.surface: Bags are tipped over onto a seat without arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacks' looks like a noun for bags, but here it is the verb meaning plunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A stool is a seat with no back or arm rests, typically on legs.

clue.text: A complete entity would make it green

indicators.note: to make something of letters is to build a new word from them, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A puzzling claim that wholeness turns things green.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, and in its older sense a thing complete in itself rather than a fraction.

clue.text: Musical entertainment, The Ring, accepted by a king and a libertine

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken in, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king, plus a as written; the order king then a follows the letters
a rake is a dissolute man of loose morals
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An opera evening at Wagner's Ring cycle, attended by royalty and a debauchee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' suggests Wagner's opera cycle, which suits 'musical entertainment', but it is only a ring-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is a pastime in which people sing along to recorded backing tracks, a form of musical entertainment.

clue.text: Go-between is to bury me with a journal

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
taken as written
a diary is a personal journal

explanation.surface: A messenger is instructed to bury the speaker along with their diary.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary is a person who acts as a link or mediator between two parties.

clue.text: Any number unwell? Could be catching!

blocks.note: n stands for an unspecified number in maths
ailing means sick

explanation.surface: Is anyone ill? It might be contagious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching' looks like 'infectious', which fits the sickly surface, but it means seizing or nabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail a culprit is to catch or trap them, so nailing means catching in the sense of seizing.

clue.text: Boast more than this: not in back-to-front dress

indicators.note: back-to-front means the end comes first, so the word is read the wrong way round

blocks.note: out is the opposite of in
garb is clothing

explanation.surface: Someone swaggers about wearing their clothes the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbrag someone is to outdo them in bragging, exceeding their boasts.

clue.text: Potter's Field!

blocks.note: surface reading: a potter's field, the biblical burial ground for strangers bought with Judas's silver
setter's reading: the subject area of the writer Stephen Potter

explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter wrote humorous books on winning games by dubious psychological ploys without actually cheating; his 'field' is the art he named.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamesmanship, the art of winning by unsporting but legal tricks, was popularised by Stephen Potter's 1947 book of that title.

clue.text: More vacant English MP goes to the bank

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written
a tier is a row or bank, as of seats

explanation.surface: An English politician heads to the bank, leaving things emptier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but it means a row or rank, like a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptier is the comparative of empty, meaning holding less, which matches 'more vacant'.

clue.text: The French man at wedding needing space

blocks.note: le is a French word for the
the groom is the man getting married

explanation.surface: A French bridegroom wants some room at the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Legroom is the room available for one's legs when seated, as in a car or aircraft.

clue.text: Gaelic girl wants jazz music after a moment

indicators.note: after sends the music to follow the short wait named behind it, reversing their clue order

blocks.note: mo is short for moment, as in 'half a mo'
rag is ragtime, an early jazz style

explanation.surface: A Highland lass asks for jazz after a short wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Morag is a Scottish female name, the Gaelic form of Sarah.

clue.text: They watch old boy taking on tennis players

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
players who serve the ball

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy takes on a group of tennis players.
explanation.definitionFit: Observers are people who look on or monitor events, so they are watchers.

clue.text: Pouch holds joint of meat given to ugly woman

blocks.note: a saddle is a cut of meat from the back, as of lamb
bag is a derogatory slang word for an unattractive woman

explanation.surface: A bag contains a cut of meat handed to an unattractive woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds' suggests a container, but nothing goes inside anything; it just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddlebag is a pouch or bag hung from a saddle or bicycle seat.

clue.text: Stupid twit did me wrong

indicators.note: doing something wrong puts it out of order, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A dim-witted fool has wronged the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim-witted describes someone slow to understand, which is a synonym for stupid.

clue.text: Indiana's here, where dew and mist are mingled

indicators.note: things mingled are mixed together, so their letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A misty, dewy morning in the American heartland.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the US states in the region of the American interior known as the Midwest.

clue.text: How to cook pork, we hear, for a man in clique

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: pork is often braised in cider

explanation.surface: A recipe tip for pork, offered to a member of an inner circle.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is someone within a group or organisation with privileged access, a member of a clique.

clue.text: Retiring Josephine dipped into dry Spanish wine

indicators.note: something dipped into another goes inside it
retiring means going back, so the combined letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: to air clothes is to dry them
Jo is a short form of Josephine

explanation.surface: A shy Josephine sips a dry Spanish wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like it describes Josephine alone, but it reverses the whole result after she is put inside; 'dry' is a verb, as in drying washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Do a turn, dancing round, in circular building

indicators.note: dancing round suggests whirling movement, so the letters spin into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A performer twirls around inside a domed hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building or hall, typically topped by a dome.

clue.text: Reporting a hundred short, no longer useful

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: news coverage is the reporting of events
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A news report is a hundred short and now outdated.
explanation.walkthrough: COVERAGE loses its C to leave OVERAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-age means past the permitted or useful age, so too old to serve its purpose.

clue.text: To say more is supported by this essayist

blocks.note: to add is to say something further
taken as written
something resting on another is supported by it

explanation.surface: An essayist backs the urge to say more.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison was an English essayist who co-founded The Spectator in 1711.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison is famed as an essayist, writing for The Spectator and The Tatler.

clue.text: Italian architect from a greener village

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the letters are lifted from inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across greener and village

explanation.surface: An Italian architect comes from a leafier village.
explanation.definitionFit: Pier Luigi Nervi was a twentieth-century Italian engineer and architect known for reinforced concrete structures.

clue.text: The ABC of literature?

blocks.note: first meaning: the characters of the alphabet
second meaning: learning and writing

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like asking for the basics of literature; instead the alphabet and literature are two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphabet is made of these characters, and the same plural also means literature or learning, as in arts and letters.

clue.text: "I surrender", says fielder with new cap

indicators.note: a new cap means a fresh top, so the first letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: a cricket or baseball player in the field

explanation.surface: A fielder in a new cap throws in the towel.
explanation.walkthrough: The F at the head of FIELDER is replaced with a Y; the clue does not clue the new letter, which the definition supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: A yielder is one who gives way or submits, the sort of person who says 'I surrender'.

clue.text: Bangle I smashed: what language!

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into bits that can be reassembled differently

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a bracelet and swears loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What language!' sounds like a reaction to cursing; language is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the language spoken in Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal.

clue.text: Racecourse leveller gets giant rat moving

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A huge rat scurrying across a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A starting gate holds all horses in a line so they begin together, evening up the start of a race.
